premises.text: Online gaming is static and anonymous—no control over who you play with; women often avoid mics due to harassment
premises.evidence_span: You don't know who you're playing with. You're dealing with anonymous gamer tags

premises.text: Game Crush offers rich profiles, blogs, pictures, chat, videos, and optional gameplay in a fun, inviting, secure place to meet gamers
premises.evidence_span: We offer rich user profiles, deep engagements with other users, including profiles that include blogs, pictures, and you're able to chat online

premises.text: Payers pay play dates who earn money playing; respectful ratings and invite control address supply/demand and safety
premises.evidence_span: The payer, as we call it, pays, and the play date actually makes money playing that game

premises.text: UI supports Flash games on-site or console games off-site with tips during play
premises.evidence_span: We have a number of Flash games available on our UI, or you can go off and play console games on your own

value.text: Meet and play with real gamers in a controlled, social, monetized environment—like buying someone a drink online
value.evidence_span: If you can buy a girl a drink in a sports bar, why can't you buy a girl a game online?

secondary_value.text: Higher payouts for game developers than traditional ad CPMs
secondary_value.evidence_span: we can pay out much greater than the CPMs you get in traditional advertising models

causal_links.evidence_span: There's no way to control your gameplay or who you play with
It offers greater control of your environment and monetarily addresses the issues of supply and demand

notes: Anonymous tags + harassment mic problem folded as one online-play social failure (§4.1.6). Profiles/engagement, payer/play-date economics, and Flash/console play surfaces folded as one platform mechanism (§4.1.7). Viral 10k users excluded as traction (§4.2). Developer CPM claim as secondary_value.
